title: Objects and dictionaries
summary: Store values under names (keys), look them up, count with them, and loop over them.

sections.heading: Values stored under names
body: An object (a dict in Python) maps keys to values. Instead of a position, you use a name to read or change a value.

javascript.code:
const person = { name: 'Ada', age: 36 }
console.log(person.name)
person.age = 37
console.log(person)

typescript.code:
const person: { name: string; age: number } = { name: 'Ada', age: 36 }
console.log(person.name)
person.age = 37
console.log(person)

sections.heading: Counting things
body: To count, use the thing as the key. If the key is not there yet, start from 0.
When the key is in a variable, use square brackets: `counts[ch]`. Writing `counts.ch` would look for a key literally called "ch".

sections.heading: Looping over keys and values
body: `Object.entries` in JavaScript and `.items()` in Python give you each key with its value.

mistakes: Using `obj.key` when the key is stored in a variable. Use `obj[key]`.
In Python, reading a missing key with `d[key]` raises `KeyError`. Use `d.get(key, default)`.
`if (counts[k])` is false when the count is 0. Check `k in counts` instead.
